output.brief: The wrong dates were not caused by the agency operators or the printer firmware. Printer job records show every job from 4 Oct 22:10 received a 36-month shelf life from PackBridge, with no operator overrides. The same happened on Line 1 day shift with permanent staff. Jobs before that, including those after the firmware change and run by agency operators, were correct. The ERP shows Regulatory Affairs entered 36 months for Veltranol on 3 Oct, but only valid from 1 Mar 2027. The 24-month value is still the one in effect. The vendor says PackBridge can't send a future value, yet it evidently did. Why is still unexplained. The camera only compares print to job data, so it passed everything. Don't warn or remove the agency operators, and keep the camera check on. Do now: reset the Veltranol shelf-life record, extend the hold to all Veltranol lots since 4 Oct (including the two on Line 1 in the warehouse), and add a second-person check of printed expiry against the batch record at each setup. Inspect other products whose records changed in October, especially the two with future valid-from dates. Ask Corvane and IT to explain how PackBridge read the future value. Confidence is high on cause and moderate on how far it spreads.
